title: OpaqueKey cache + 429 investigation labbook
content:
Notes to self: summing up the recent flurry of 429/401 reports from mobile beta and a couple of enterprise tenants. Trying to keep an ordered labbook so I can hand off to SRE if needed.

Summary of observed behavior:
- Several clients reported 429 bursts followed by 401s for the same API key within ~90s window.
- Pattern: heavy concurrent traffic -> many 429s with Retry-After present -> after clients backoff, some requests start returning 401 when hitting different gateway nodes.
- Not universal: some keys never saw 401 even under same load. Suspect cache / rotation edge-case.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) API-key validation caching bug in the inference-gateway: cached "good" key state expires or is evicted inconsistently and some nodes reject with 401 when they missed a rotation/refresh.
2) Quota enforcement has a two-stage flow: fast path returns 429 from front proxy (per-node window) while backend marks key as over-quota and also rotates an ephemeral marker; if subsequent request hits a node that expects the rotated marker it might treat the token as stale -> 401.
3) Clock-skew / TTL mismatch between auth service and gateway causing intermittent "token expired" 401s after a quota event.
4) Client-side: some SDKs aggressively rotate or re-request keys on 429 and then send malformed Authorization header (missing Bearer or extra quotes) leading to 401s.

What I've tried so far (repro + debugging commands):
- Repro script: spawn 200 concurrent curl workers hitting /v1/generate with same key for 60s (local). Example curl worker used:
  curl -s -D - \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"input":"hi"}' \n    https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate | sed -n '1,15p'

- Observed response headers during repro: (copied from a test run)
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  x-rate-limit-limit: 120
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
  Retry-After: 30
  Date: Fri, 08 Nov 2024 15:02:11 GMT

  Follow-up after backing off (same workload, different node):
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="redwood", error="invalid_token", error_description="key not found"

- Gateway logs (filtered):
  kubectl -n prod logs deployment/inference-gateway --tail=500 | rg 'key-hash: abc123' -n
  Found sequences where node A accepted validation at t=0, node B returned 401 at t=2s with message "cache-miss -> remote-validate failed".

- Auth service traces (jaeger):
  Trace shows a ValidateKey RPC that returned success for the key, but there were intermittent 500s in validate-key-store during the burst window (~3% error rate). When validate-store 500s occurred, gateway returned 401 immediately.

- Check for SDK/client misbehavior:
  - Mobile SDK (v0.9.2): on 429 the client retries immediately with exponential backoff but also refreshes stored key if it sees a 401. The refresh path was returning the same key (no new key), but client code strips whitespace incorrectly in some conditions -> malformed header observed in logs (Authorization:Bearer<token> no space).
  - Server-side curl tests do not reproduce malformed header. So client is a contributor but not sole cause.

Quick reproducer steps for SRE to run:
1) export API_KEY=<problem-key>
2) ./stress-sender --concurrency 150 --duration 60 --url https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate --header "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY"
3) tail -f kubectl -n prod logs deployment/inference-gateway | rg "$API_KEY_SHORT"
4) correlate with jaeger trace ids shown in gateway logs and inspect validate-key-service logs around those trace ids.

Observations about headers and quota shapes:
- We publish x-rate-limit-* on 429s but not reliably on 401s. That makes it hard for clients to decide backoff after 401.
- Some 401s include WWW-Authenticate with error_description "key not found" which implies gateway treated the key as unknown rather than expired. Might be caused by partial writes to the key-store during rotation.

Immediate mitigations tried (short-term):
- Patch deployed to gateway to add a 2-second retry to remote-validate on transient 5xx from validate-key-store (safe: idempotent). Canary to 10% nodes. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
- Reverted a recent change in mobile SDK where it aggressively refreshed stored key on 429s (rolled back to v0.9.1 for the beta cohort).

Data we still need / next diagnostic actions:
- [ ] Collect list of keys that saw both 429 and 401 within 2 minutes. (SRE: query logs with key-hash grouping)
- [ ] Add metric around validate-key-store latency and 5xx rate with 1s granularity during next rolling window.
- [ ] Ensure gateway emits x-rate-limit-* and Retry-After for 401s that are quota-related (if any). Add a field to indicate "auth-failure-reason" in logs.
- [ ] Check KMS/HSM rotation schedule for keys used by validate-key-store (possible TTL mismatch).
- [ ] Get packet captures or tcpdump for a failing window if we need to prove malformed header in transit.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Move to single consistent validate-key-store (or strongly-consistent cache) instead of per-node approximate caching for API keys used in enterprise plans.
- Introduce a grace window after quota enforcement where existing cached validations remain valid for N seconds to avoid 401s triggered by asynchronous quota marking.
- Improve client SDK header sanitation and stricter validation on client before sending Authorization header.

Notes / unsorted breadcrumbs:
- LIN-987 has the customer-reported timeline and contains mobile logs (attached).
- Related PR 1234 is the small retry-on-5xx fix for gateway -> validate-store. Might help but not full root cause.
- Slack thread infra-ops: thread GMK3J2K1 has a heatmap of 429 spikes by region. In EMEA the pattern is less pronounced, suggests routing variation.

Quick checklist for handoff to SRE on-call:
1) Run reproducer with key X (I put the key in the Linear ticket).
2) Collect logs from inference-gateway, validate-key-store (past 10 minutes) and jaeger traces.
3) Confirm whether validate-store returned 5xx correlated with 401s.
4) If 401s coincide with validate-store 5xx, keep canary patch and escalate to roll to 100% (we need the retry behavior in gateway).
5) If 401s occur without validate-store 5xx, collect tcpdump and check client headers.

To do next (my tasks):
- Follow up with mobile SDK owner about header serialization bug (Marco).
- Add small logging change to gateway to include a compact key-hash in each auth log line for faster grepping.
- Draft a short postmortem template if this escalates to a SEV: timeline, impact, root cause, mitigation, long-term plan.

End notes: keep this file as my scratch pad. Do not push as-is to Confluence. If we get a SEV I will move final timeline to shared_drives/company/misc/postmortems.
